newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 7.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 7. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto has given Women's Affairs Minister Mien Sugandhi permission to visit the Middle East to talk with Indonesian women working there as prostitutes.
Lieutenant-General Wiranto, head of the military's strategic reserve, has said recent rioting in Indonesia was the result of a lack of disciplined principles among the people.
Eight sub-organisations of the 30-million-strong Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) have warned that the recent flurry of religious and ethnic riots reflected waning public trust in the government.
The Directorate General of Customs and Excise has assured business people that imports will be cleared faster when it regains its inspection authority starting April 1.
Police have admitted that a South African man detained for smuggling morphine has escaped from custody.
Only Indonesians will be allowed buy shares in the company set up to finance the development of the N-2130 passenger jet being built by state planemaker IPTN.
